input.content: # GIF Editor — UI/UX revamp (branch `ui-improvements`) ## Context The app works, but it feels like a prototype: - Emoji icons and ad-hoc Tailwind classes repeated in every tool. - A full-screen blocking modal for every operation and for engine loading. - Undo is slow: it replays FFmpeg operations. It is also buggy: undo after a Frames edit silently drops that edit, because `replayOperation` has no `frames` case. - No way to pause or scrub the GIF. - Number-only trim inputs. - Mouse-only crop. - Ctrl+Z only, and it hijacks inputs. - Every download is named `edited.gif`. The user asked for a revamp of the whole UI and UX. Choices they confirmed: - **Visual direction:** friendly and playful. - **Use case:** general editing and Slack export are **equal peers**. - **In scope:** live previews, instant undo/redo, playback controls, power-user flow. Stack stays the same: vanilla JS ES modules, Tailwind v4, FFmpeg.wasm, Vite. No framework migration. ## Design direction: "friendly and playful" - **Tokens:** Tailwind v4 `@theme` semantic colors (`surface`, `surface-2`, `ink`, `muted`, `line`, `accent` plus per-tool accent hues) backed by CSS vars, with `@custom-variant dark`. These replace the `t-*` helper classes in `src/styles/custom.css`. - **Theme:** defaults to the system theme. The toggle cycles light → dark → system and is stored in localStorage. - **Shapes and type:** large radii (`rounded-2xl`), soft shadows, springy micro-animations (scale on press, bounce on drop). Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Font:** a rounded display font, self-hosted via `@fontsource-variable/nunito`. Google Fonts would be blocked by COEP `require-corp`. - **Icons:** a small inlined SVG set (Lucide paths, ISC) in `src/ui/icons.js`, each tool with its own color chip. Emoji are kept only as personality accents in empty states, not as functional icons. - **Layout:** - **Desktop:** header, left tool rail, center stage, right options panel. - **Mobile:** stage on top, a scrollable tool-chip bar at the bottom, and options in a bottom sheet. ## Implementation (in order; one commit per step) ### 1. Foundation - `src/styles/custom.css`: rewrite as the token system, plus a checkerboard utility, slider/segmented/button styles, and focus rings. Keep the existing WCAG contrast notes. - `src/ui/icons.js` (new): `icon(name, cls)` returns an SVG string. - `src/ui/components.js` (new): small HTML-string helpers used by every tool panel: - `button({variant, icon, label})` - `sliderField({id, label, min, max, step, value, format})` - `segmented({id, options})` - `numberField` - `panelHeader({title, icon, color, hint})` This removes the duplicated class strings in the `src/tools/*.js` panels. - `index.html`: new shell with these parts: - header: logo, filename chip, undo/redo, Export menu, theme, GitHub - landing - editor (tool rail, stage, options panel, history) - batch view - toast region - `` elements for shortcuts The unsupported-browser banner stays. ### 2. State and history: instant undo/redo - `src/utils/state.js`: - Replace `operations`/`checkpoints`/`pushOperation`/`popOperation` with snapshot history `{ entries: [{label, gif, meta}], index }`. - New functions: `commit(label, gif)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `jumpTo(i)`. - Cap at about 30 entries or about 256 MB total, dropping the oldest. Entry 0 (the original) is always kept. - `src/main.js`: delete `replayOperation` and the checkpoint undo logic. Revert becomes `jumpTo(0)`. - `src/components/history.js` (new): a clickable history list in the options panel, plus undo/redo buttons in the header with disabled states. ### 3. Shared tool runner and tool registry - `src/tools/shared.js`: add `runFFmpegJob({label, inputs, commands, output, cleanup})`. It wraps the write → exec (one or more passes) → read → delete pattern that every tool currently repeats. Wire it to `commit()`, toasts and progress. - `src/components/toolbar.js`: turn the hardcoded `tools` array into a registry. Each tool registers `{id, label, icon, color, hotkey, render(panel), enter(), exit()}`. `enter`/`exit` let tools set up and tear down live previews and overlays, which replaces the crop-canvas and frame-strip special cases in `selectTool`. - Each `src/tools/*.js` file is migrated to the registry and the shared runner, which shrinks it noticeably. ### 4. Stage: player, zoom, compare, progress - `src/components/player.js` (new): - **Playback:** a canvas player using WebCodecs `ImageDecoder`, with play/pause, frame step, a scrubber, a frame counter, and a playback-rate hook. - **Fallback:** if `ImageDecoder` isn't available, it shows a plain `` and hides the playback controls. - **Zoom:** Fit, 100%, and +/- zoom, with `image-rendering: pixelated` above 100%, on a checkerboard background. - **Compare:** a "Compare" control that you hold, or toggle with `\`, shows the original (entry 0) against the current GIF. The metadata bar shows the size delta, e.g. `412 KB → 188 KB (−54%)`. - `src/ffmpeg/engine.js`: - **Preload:** the engine starts loading in the background as soon as a GIF loads. - **Status pill:** loading progress is published to state (`engine: {status, pct}`) and shown as a header pill instead of the `ffmpeg-loader` modal. The pill blocks only if you apply a tool before the engine is ready. - **Job progress:** wire `ffmpeg.on('progress')` into the job overlay, which now covers only the stage, not the whole app. It falls back to an indeterminate bar. ### 5. Tool panels with live previews - **Filters:** live CSS `filter` approximation on the stage while you drag the sliders, labelled "preview ≈". Presets become visual swatch thumbnails. - **Speed:** a live preview through the player's playback rate. It shows the new duration. - **Reverse:** a "Preview" button that plays the decoded frames backwards before you apply. - **Trim:** `src/components/trim-timeline.js` (new) is a dual-handle range over a filmstrip, using player frames or delay-proportional segments. Add quick presets (Light / Balanced / Tiny). - **Resize:** a proper lock toggle button. Presets as segmented controls, plus a "Fit 128" preset. - **Frames:** - Prefill the output FPS from the GIF's real fps instead of a hardcoded 10. - Bigger thumbnails, with multi-select delete and keyboard reorder. - Revoke the frame URLs on tool exit (they currently leak). ### 6. Export, landing, batch - **Export:** a header split button. The primary action is Download. The menu holds "Slack emoji" and a live 128 KB budget hint. Downloads use the original name: `cat.gif` becomes `cat-edited.gif` (fix in `src/components/export-panel.js`, using `fileName` from state). - **Landing:** a playful hero with an animated drop target and two equal cards ("Edit a GIF" / "Batch Slack emoji"). It also carries a privacy line ("never leaves your device") and a paste hint. - **Batch:** a revamp of `src/components/batch.js`: - per-card status pills with spinners - an overall progress bar - per-item download and before/after size - a "Download .zip" button - existing logic kept: `uniqueName`, `escapeHtml`, `zipSync` with level 0 - **Toasts:** move toasts to bottom-center, with icons, a close button, and an `aria-live` region kept. ### 7. Power-user flow - `src/components/shortcuts.js` (new): - `1–8` select a tool, `Esc` closes the tool, `Space` plays/pauses. - `,` and `.` step frames, `⌘/Ctrl+Z` undoes, `⌘/Ctrl+Shift+Z` redoes, `⌘/Ctrl+S` downloads. - `\` compares, `?` opens the cheat-sheet ``. - Shortcuts are ignored while focus is in an input. - Drop or paste (Ctrl+V) a GIF anywhere, at any time, through a full-window drop overlay. One GIF replaces the current one, after confirming if there is history. Several GIFs open batch. `filterGifs`/`openBatch` from `batch.js` are reused. - README: update the Features list and add a Shortcuts section. ## Reused as-is - `src/ffmpeg/commands.js`, all builders - `src/tools/slack-emoji.js` - `src/utils/gif-info.js`, whose `delays` feed the trim timeline and fps - `src/utils/file-utils.js` - `filterGifs` / `uniqueName` in `src/components/batch.js` - the IndexedDB WASM cache in `engine.js` ## Verification No test suite exists, so verification is build checks plus driving the app in a browser: 1. **Build:** `npm run build` succeeds with no warnings about missing modules. 2. **Drive the app:** `npm run dev`, then use the `run` / claude-in-chrome skills. - **Landing:** load a GIF via click, drag-drop and paste. - **Engine pill:** the pill shows progress without blocking. - **Tools:** apply every tool. Live previews react while dragging, and crop works with a touch emulator. - **History:** undo/redo is instant and correct after a Frames edit (the regression check for the old bug). Clicking history entries jumps between states, and Compare shows the original. - **Player:** play/pause, step, scrub, and zoom up to pixelated 400%. - **Export:** Download produces `-edited.gif`. Slack export lands at ≤128 KB. - **Batch:** drop 3 or more GIFs. Statuses and progress update, and the zip contains the original names. - **Shortcuts:** every key works, `?` opens the dialog, and shortcuts are inert while typing in inputs. 3. **Theme and responsive:** light, dark and system themes. A 375px-wide viewport (bottom sheet, no horizontal scroll). Keyboard-only navigation with visible focus. 4. **Fallback:** Firefox, or with `ImageDecoder` stubbed out. The `` fallback renders and playback controls hide cleanly.

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

content.text:
The redesign is finished and committed on `ui-improvements` (`edef8a2`) but not pushed. I ran the app in headless Chromium against generated test GIFs. Every tool, undo/redo, compare, both exports, batch, the shortcuts, a 375px phone layout, dark mode and the fallback without `ImageDecoder` all worked, with no console errors.

**Look:** a friendly, playful style with a warm cream or deep violet background, a rounded font, colorful chips for each tool, and a gradient wordmark. The theme can be light, dark, or follow the system setting.

**Layout:**
- **Landing page:** two equal paths, "Edit a GIF" and "Batch Slack emoji", plus a note that files never leave your device.
- **Editor:** tool rail on the left, the GIF in the middle, options on the right, and a clickable history list.
- **Phone:** tools sit along the bottom and options open in a bottom sheet.

**New in the editor:**
- **Player:** play/pause, step through frames, scrub, zoom up to 800% with crisp pixels, and a side-by-side compare with the original that shows the size change.
- **Instant undo/redo:** each edit is kept as a snapshot, so you can jump to any step. This fixes an old bug where undoing after a Frames edit silently dropped that edit.
- **Live previews:**
  - **Filters:** applied to the playing GIF as you drag.
  - **Speed:** plays at the new speed.
  - **Reverse:** plays backwards.
  - **Trim:** a filmstrip with drag handles that loops your selection.
  - **Crop:** works with touch and has edge handles.
- **Background engine loading:** the engine starts loading as soon as a GIF is opened, with progress in a small header pill. While an edit runs, only the GIF area is covered.
- **Shortcuts:** `1`–`8` open tools, `Space` plays/pauses, `,`/`.` step, `\` compares, `⌘Z`/`⌘⇧Z` undo/redo, `⌘S` downloads, `?` lists them all. They don't fire while you're typing in a field.
- **Drop or paste a GIF anywhere**, at any time.

**Smaller fixes:**
- Downloads are named after the original file (`cat-edited.gif`) instead of `edited.gif`.
- The Slack export result is now part of the undo history.
- Batch export shows per-file progress and download buttons, and doesn't redo files it has already optimized.
- Rebuilt frames now use a proper color palette, so they look better.
- The compress frame-rate slider no longer misreports "original".

**Changed from the plan:**
- The header has two equal buttons, **Slack emoji** and **Download**, instead of a dropdown. That fit "both equally" better.
- Icons come from the `lucide` package and the font from `@fontsource-variable/nunito`. Those are the two new dependencies.
- Everything is in one commit rather than one per step, because the pieces were built together.

**Limits:**
- The live filter preview is a close approximation of the final colors, and the panel says so.
- Frame stepping and the reverse and trim previews need the browser's frame decoder. Without it the app shows a plain animated image and hides the player controls, as tested. Very large GIFs skip the reverse preview to save memory.
- I tested only with GIFs I generated and only in Chromium. Firefox and some real-world GIFs are worth a manual check before merging.
